cause_quote: The new background child ran `require("node:fs").rmSync(process.argv[1], { recursive: true, force: true })`, deleting the entire retired tree in one recursive operation without yielding to foreground writers.
user_saw: Chat transcript writes were delayed by several seconds while a large retired worktree was being deleted on btrfs.
summary: Linux retired-worktree cleanup now yields after 30 seconds or when the pressure probe detects a slow btrfs commit, then resumes after a quiet interval.
reasoning: I checked the introducing diff and confirmed that #169690 moved retired-tree deletion into a background child that could generate filesystem metadata work for an entire tree without yielding. The later batching and reservation checks reduced pressure but still allowed a long deletion below the reservation watermark. The reported stall occurred after those mitigations, so its severity on the original implementation is unverified.
